title: Building the engine model, one verified layer at a time.
summary: A verified Python foundation, an earlier engine-solver roadmap and the work still needed to connect geometry, physics and measurements. Software checks come first; a complete engine twin remains a development goal.
dateLabel: 18 Oct 2026 · Python gate review; earlier roadmap retained
evidence: Accepted nominal software checks · physical validation pending
heroAlt: Software evidence sequence: frozen inputs, accepted nominal Python checks, Rhino integration not run and future physical calibration.
heroCaption: Evidence sequence, not an engine-performance plot. The Python gate qualifies nominal software checks; actual Rhino integration has not run and physical calibration remains future work.

sections.title: One foundation, several kinds of model
sections.text: The target is a digital twin of the entire engine. The accepted first layer is smaller: a Wahoo-owned, backend-independent Python foundation for nominal motion, geometry and evidence handling. It does not replace a combustion or engine-performance solver. Rhino remains authoritative for spatial geometry; actual integration is still untested in the reviewed acceptance record.

figure.alt: Accepted Python foundation separated from proposed Rhino geometry, physics-backend and measurement connections.
figure.caption: Solid stages describe the existing software foundation. Dashed connections are future integrations; this is an architecture diagram, not a demonstrated coupled twin.

sections.title: Start with motion we can trace
sections.text: The historical motion model uses nominal rigid bodies, zero cylinder offset and constant angular speed. The graph reuses all 361 original one-degree samples. It shows piston travel and signed velocity, with no fitted or smoothed curve. The 12,000 rpm source reference is a design example, not a safe operating limit or a measured engine run.

figure.alt: Two plots of piston travel in millimetres and signed piston velocity in metres per second against crank angle from 0 to 360 degrees.
figure.caption: Frozen historical samples, reproduced unchanged as connected points. Travel and velocity are positive toward the crankshaft. Nominal dimensions and actual mechanical interfaces remain unverified.

sections.title: What passed the Python gate
sections.text: On 18 October, 21 admission checks passed. The final suite recorded 542 passes, no failures and one Rhino integration check not run. It covered historical motion, 54 parameter combinations, derivative convergence, cold-volume semantics, units and frames, invalid inputs and reproducibility. Two test-recording defects were repaired while retaining failed attempts; equations and acceptance thresholds were not relaxed.

figure.alt: Eight software-check categories total 542 passes, with Rhino A6 separately labelled not run.
figure.caption: Accepted final-suite counts. They count software checks, including related cases; they are not independent physical experiments or a confidence percentage.

sections.title: Keep the earlier solver roadmap in view
sections.text: The earlier roadmap investigated a Wahoo interface around licensed EngMod2T. Static documentation and example-file review supported further investigation; they did not demonstrate a Wahoo performance run or vendor integration. Internal-stinger modelling still needs mapping to Wahoo’s straight exhaust. Port/scavenging assumptions and the annular-rim piston representation require review. Trial activation and unattended integration are not established by the Python gate.

sections.title: Preserve the foundation as it moves
sections.text: An accepted 18 October migration established a dedicated simulator home, explicit local execution and verified synchronization. The same nominal regression passed again: 542 passes, no failures, Rhino not run. Separately, 39 storage checks passed and 245 inventoried originals remained unchanged. Original packages provide rollback; shared engine/CAD sources keep their own authority. This qualifies relocation and preservation, without adding physics capability.

sections.title: A pass at one layer is not a pass at every layer
sections.text: The accepted scope is nominal rigid, zero-offset cold geometry. Synthetic chamber-volume examples are software fixtures. Actual chamber measurements, assembly mapping, physical rotation, hot clearance and Rhino compatibility remain open. Power, combustion, safe engine speed, temperatures and manufacturing readiness are not validated.

figure.alt: Four evidence layers distinguish accepted nominal software, checked relocation, untested actual CAD connection and unvalidated physical engine behaviour.
figure.caption: Software and storage checks preserve a useful foundation. CAD roundtrips, measured geometry and physical engine tests must earn their own evidence.

sections.title: The next useful comparisons
sections.text: Future engine/exhaust comparisons should use source-qualified inputs, packaging and propulsion-load constraints, conservation and convergence checks, and sensitivity to uncertain inputs. Complete ECU behaviour, coolant flow and detailed metal temperatures need their own models and measurements; prescribed inputs cannot substitute for them. Bench and dyno evidence must eventually calibrate and challenge predictions. These are development requirements, not completed simulations.
